from: kbf v0.0.64 (8f90d0604794f3fee057e71647c7e1c1e034fa2e): every struct the coordinator reads from its state files, in kbf-coordinator/src/desired.rs (the desired state), ops.rs (the ops file) and ops_file.rs (the halts file beside it), and the report inside them, kbf-updater/src/wire.rs and wire_report.rs. `files` names the struct each state file is read with. For a struct, `source` is where it is at the tag, `allowed` are the keys it has, `required` the ones without a serde default (an Option field without `default` is not required either) and `schema` the schema it reads. `lenient` is true for a struct kbf reads without deny_unknown_fields, which skips a key it does not know: the halts file, the records in it and the report; every other struct refuses one. A record of the halts file that kbf cannot read is passed over with its report lost, and the rest of the file is read; the mirror counts such a record as refused, since a file this coordinator writes should lose nothing. `nested` is the shape of the value of a key that is a struct: `T` a struct, `[T]` an array of them, `{T}` a map from names to them. `types` is the type of the value of every other allowed key, one of: `string`; `u32` and `u64` (a JSON integer, not negative, that fits); `version` (a string that kbf-updater's Version::parse takes: a digit first, then letters, digits and . + ~ -, at most 128 bytes); `token` (1 to 64 bytes of a-z, 0-9 and _, kbf-updater's Token); `enum:a|b|c` (a string that is one of the serde spellings); `limits` (a map from a role name to a count of at most 10000, as Desired::checked takes max_updating and min_up; a role name is a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 32 bytes, none last); `min_up` (limits that name storage and frontend, which Desired::checked requires of the state of kbf; this coordinator names them in every state it writes); `map<string,V>` and `[V]` (a map and an array of values of the type V, any type above). `nullable` lists the keys whose value may be null: the fields kbf reads as an Option (or leniently), where null is none. A null in any other allowed key is refused, a required one included, as serde refuses it for a map, a list or a count that has a default and is no Option; so is a null report of a halt in the halts file, which kbf passes over. The phase, class and reason of a report are read as none by kbf when it does not know the value; the mirror holds them to the spellings, since a value outside them is one kbf drops.
